title: High Talent Wants the Latitude to Tackle Big Challenges
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that treating your most talented team members the same as everyone else is a fast way to lose them. It recommends giving high performers meaty challenges, then setting clear guidelines and getting out of the way rather than overmanaging their execution. The article notes leaders often default to giving the biggest projects to their most experienced people, missing the chance to stretch high-potential talent before they're 'ready.' The overarching message: talented people want latitude and risk, not just recognition.
points: Treating highly talented team members like everyone else is a fast path to losing them.
Once a tough assignment is given, the best leaders set guidelines, define success, and step back.
Overmanaging a talented team member's execution is described as 'the kiss of death.'
Leaders often default to giving big projects to the most experienced people, overlooking high-potential talent.
Giving stretch assignments before someone feels fully ready is how top leaders retain future stars.
quotes: Good leaders know that if they treat highly talented team members in the same way they engage everyone else it is a recipe for losing them.
Overmanaging the talented team member as they engage the project is the kiss of death.
They let the talented team member make their own mistakes and navigate the boat the way they want.
Too often, leaders give the biggest challenges and stretch assignments to their most experienced and trusted people.
When they have the skills to do so, the best leaders give them running shoes and let them sprint.
